Mode-centred central composite design over outer hyperparameters

Source: R/hyper_ccd.R
tulpa_ccd_outer_grid.Rd

Places the nodes of a central composite design (CCD) at the mode of an outer log-marginal and scales them by its curvature, the outer integration INLA uses (Rue, Martino and Chopin 2009). eval_logm is the caller's inner solve: the log marginal at one physical hyperparameter vector. Each axis is integrated in an unconstrained coordinate with a flat prior there, the log of a positive scale or the value of a bounded parameter, and its physical box bounds the mode-find and clamps the nodes. The design reuses ccd_grid(), ccd_to_theta() and ccd_weights(), and the outer PSIS k-hat of the Gaussian proposal comes from tulpa_batched_pareto_k().

Usage

tulpa_ccd_outer_grid(
  eval_logm,
  axes,
  f0_mult = 1.1,
  diagnose_k = TRUE,
  k_samples = .nl_diag("ccd_k_samples"),
  max_modefind = 40L
)

Arguments

eval_logm

function(theta) returning the log marginal (a scalar) at the physical hyperparameter vector theta (axes in axes order), or a non-finite value where it is not defined.

axes

List of axes, each list(name, log_scale, lower, upper, start): log_scale = TRUE integrates log(theta); lower / upper is the physical box; start the physical starting value of the mode-find.

f0_mult

Multiplier on the design radius sqrt(k).

diagnose_k

Compute the outer PSIS k-hat.

k_samples

Proposal draws for the k-hat.

max_modefind

Iteration cap of the bounded mode-find (each step is one inner solve per coordinate).

Value

A list with ok; when TRUE also nodes (n_node x k physical values, columns named), dnode (design weights), u_hat and L (mode and Cholesky factor of the outer covariance in the unconstrained coordinates), kind (per-node label), n_points, pareto_k; when FALSE, reason.

Details

The design declines (returning ok = FALSE with the reason) when there are fewer than two axes (a one-dimensional grid is cheaper and as accurate), when the mode-find fails or lands on the box, or when the outer curvature is not positive definite or is ill-conditioned (a weakly identified axis); the caller then integrates on its tensor grid.

See also

tulpa_hyper_grid() (design = "ccd"), which builds the axes from its axis specs.

Examples

# A bivariate Gaussian log marginal in (log tau, rho).
f <- function(th) -0.5 * ((log(th[1]) - 1)^2 / 0.04 + (th[2] - 0.4)^2 / 0.01)
axes <- list(list(name = "tau", log_scale = TRUE, lower = 0.3, upper = 30,
                  start = 3),
             list(name = "rho", log_scale = FALSE, lower = 0.05,
                  upper = 0.95, start = 0.5))
cc <- tulpa_ccd_outer_grid(f, axes, diagnose_k = FALSE)
cc$nodes
